title: Effects of Periodization on Strength and Muscle Hypertrophy in Volume-Equated Resistance Training Programs: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
population: 35 studies in trained and untrained participants, with volume equated between conditions.
key_findings: With volume equated, periodized training gave larger 1RM gains than non-periodized training (effect size 0.31), but not more hypertrophy (0.13, interval including zero).
Undulating periodization gave larger 1RM gains than linear (0.31), driven by trained participants (0.61); in untrained participants they were similar.
Linear and undulating periodization gave similar hypertrophy.
methods: Systematic review and inverse-variance random-effects meta-analyses of non-periodized versus periodized and linear versus undulating training, with subgroups by training status.
limitations: Other periodization models could not be meta-analysed for lack of studies; the neural explanation offered for the strength effect is the authors' proposal.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
